correctness.rationale: The theorem is correct. For any chosen maximal square minor, the clustered exponential determinant has leading term (i epsilon)^{r(r-1)/2} V(a)V(theta)/prod(q!), so the minor is a nonzero real-analytic function in either the selected delays or selected angles. Rank deficiency forces that minor to vanish; the zero set of a nontrivial real-analytic function has Lebesgue measure zero. The rectangular cases, unused parameters, half-open angular boundary, and r=1 case do not change the conclusion. The clustered-delay argument also correctly shows that full rank does not give a uniform positive least-singular-value bound.

originality.rationale: PASS to the best of current searchable knowledge. Ng and Kutz, arXiv:2608.14001 (2026-08-14), explicitly pose the generalized-Vandermonde full-rank property as Conjecture 1 and condition their nonuniform stable-Takens result on it. A fresh search through 2026-09-29 found no later paper resolving that fixed-frequency almost-everywhere rank statement. The analytic-zero-set and Vandermonde ingredients are classical; the originality lies in closing that explicit 2026 bottleneck and formulating the conditional almost-sure consequence.

scientific_value.rationale: The result removes an explicit algebraic conjecture from a very recent nonuniform stable-linear-Takens theorem for absolutely continuous sampling laws while cleanly separating probability-one injectivity from conditioning. Resolving a named bottleneck with a short proof is scientifically useful even though the proof ingredients are standard.

independent_checks: Re-derived the Cauchy–Binet expansion of det(exp(i epsilon a_j b_p)); the unique minimum total exponent set is {0,...,r-1}, giving the stated nonzero Vandermonde coefficient.

Checked that one fixed nontrivial maximal minor suffices: rank deficiency is contained in its zero locus, and independence from unused row/column parameters still gives a measure-zero cylinder by the analytic zero-set theorem/Fubini.
Checked the fixed-delay/fixed-angle symmetry and that admissible distinct tuples are an open full-measure subset of the ambient parameter box/orthant.

Checked the conditioning limitation: clustered rows converge to identical rows as epsilon tends to zero, hence sigma_min tends to zero although the selected minor is nonzero for sufficiently small generic nonzero epsilon.
limitations: This is a generic-rank/measure-zero theorem, not deterministic full rank for every distinct delay tuple and not a quantitative conditioning theorem.
Absolute continuity is essential to the probability-one corollary; singular laws can live on aliasing sets.
Originality is source-specific: the analytic zero-set and exponential-Vandermonde expansion are standard tools, not new mathematics by themselves.

literature.note: Ng–Kutz, Stable Takens' Embedding Theorem for Non-Uniformly-Sampled Linear Systems; current abstract states the uneven-delay theorem is conditional on a generalized-Vandermonde rank conjecture.
Indexed open-problem page quoting Conjecture 1 and its distinct-positive-delay/distinct-unit-circle-node assumptions.
Recent generalized Vandermonde work in nonuniform array processing; relevant conditioning literature, but no located theorem resolving the source-specific almost-everywhere rank conjecture.
